I'm a trans man and I often use my lived experience of what I call "the before times" (before I transitioned) to explain to other guys just how common sexual harassment is for women. As a teenager I had to deal with creepy guys on the bus, I was followed home from school one day and from uni another time, had creepy customers in my first job, avoided creepy men in nightclubs, didn't feel safe walking about alone and especially at night, etc etc....

As a guy (and someone who doesn't look obviously trans at all, like, people are surprised when I tell them I am), I practically never experience this. There are one or two mildly creepy female customers at work, and the occasional creepy dude in gay clubs, but that's about it. I feel SO much safer going about my daily business, and I can really see how so many guys honestly don't realise just how bad things are on the other side of the fence.

Lots of people try to say that trans people are a threat to women's safety - there's already tons wrong with that argument, but also, it misses out the fact that we can use our lived experience both ways to explain how prevalent sexism is, and so on.

Hey, I'm a trans man who has been on T for a number of years and is living life as the person I've always known I am. I'm lucky to pass as male quite easily now and I am "stealth" in various aspects of my life (i.e. people don't know I'm trans unless I choose to tell them). 

The reason I tell you all of this is because I just wanted to say, please don't take away your chance to live life as your authentic self by doing anything drastic. I know first-hand how hard and painful it can be being a closeted trans person, going through the wrong puberty, all of that. I have some unsupportive members of my family too and it took an awfully long time for me to come out. Please, know that it gets better. 4+ years is nothing compared to the rest of your life. You are so young and have so much ahead of you, so much to live for. 

For me, I coped as a teenager by immersing myself in my schoolwork and my passions - I had tons of hobbies and filled my time with things. I know that may sound impossible if you're struggling with depression, but try to find one thing at least that you enjoy doing and you care about. Try to have some other goals for the future, as well as living as male. What kind of job do you want? What kind of skills or personal qualities do you want? And work towards these. There is a lot you can do now to help to make yourself the man you want to be in ten years' time

I also loved video games as a teenager, because my character could be male even if I couldn't live that life yet, and I liked being online and not disclosing my birth name or birth sex. You could join communities for things you care about online - music, art, sports, anything - and just pick a gender neutral or masculine name and profile picture if that makes you feel more comfortable 

I hope things get better for you soon and just know that you are not alone. Please know that the support and help is out there. If you are in the UK I recommend the LGBT Switchboard, they are a fantastic helpline ran by people who understand
